terminology.decree: Final Judgment and Decree of Divorce

residencyRequirements.description: The petitioner must have been a bona fide resident of Georgia for at least six months immediately preceding the filing of the complaint. A nonresident may file against a respondent who has been a Georgia resident for at least six months. There is no separate county residency requirement.

exceptions: The 30-day waiting period applies specifically to no-fault divorces granted on the ground that the marriage is irretrievably broken (O.C.G.A. § 19-5-3(13)). Fault-based grounds may not require this waiting period.
waitingPeriod.description: Georgia requires a mandatory 30-day waiting period after service of process on the respondent before a no-fault divorce can be finalized. This period cannot be waived by party agreement. (O.C.G.A. § 19-5-3(13))

voidabilityGrounds.name: Intermarriage Within Prohibited Degrees
voidabilityGrounds.description: Intermarriage within prohibited degrees of consanguinity or affinity
voidabilityGrounds.notes: Ground of voidability (imperfect marriage) — not a fault ground

voidabilityGrounds.name: Mental Incapacity at Time of Marriage
voidabilityGrounds.description: Mental incapacity or lunacy at the time of the marriage
voidabilityGrounds.notes: Ground of voidability — incapacity must exist at time of marriage

voidabilityGrounds.name: Impotency
voidabilityGrounds.description: Impotency at the time of the marriage
voidabilityGrounds.notes: Ground of voidability — must have existed at time of marriage and been unknown to the other party

voidabilityGrounds.name: Force, Menace, Duress, or Fraud
voidabilityGrounds.description: Force, menace, duress, or fraud in obtaining the marriage

voidabilityGrounds.name: Pregnancy of Wife by Another Man
voidabilityGrounds.description: Pregnancy of the wife by a man other than the husband at the time of the marriage, such pregnancy being unknown to the husband

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: Adultery in either of the parties after marriage

fault.name: Wilful Desertion
fault.description: Wilful and continued desertion by either of the parties for the term of one year

fault.name: Conviction of Crime Involving Moral Turpitude
fault.description: Conviction of either party for an offense involving moral turpitude and sentence of imprisonment in a penal institution for a term of two years or longer

fault.name: Cruel Treatment
fault.description: Cruel treatment, which shall consist of the willful infliction of pain, bodily or mental, upon the complaining party, such as reasonably justifies apprehension of danger to life, limb, or health

fault.name: Incurable Mental Illness
fault.description: Incurable mental illness. The mental illness must be adjudicated by a court of competent jurisdiction and confirmed by the testimony of two physicians

fault.name: Habitual Drug Addiction
fault.description: Habitual addiction to any controlled substance

propertyDivision.description: Georgia is an equitable distribution state. Marital property is divided equitably (fairly) but not necessarily equally. The court considers many factors including the contribution of each spouse, the length of the marriage, and the economic circumstances of each party.

filingFees.notes: Filing fees vary by county in Georgia, typically $200-$250. Contact the Superior Court clerk's office in your county for current fees.

basic.description: Required disclosure of income, expenses, assets, and liabilities

basic.name: Domestic Relations Case Filing Information Form
basic.description: Court administrative form required at filing

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal notice to respondent issued by the clerk

service.name: Acknowledgment of Service
service.notes: Respondent signs before a notary public acknowledging service

inState.description: Respondent must file an answer within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Georgia must file an answer within 60 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Georgia uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined to determine the basic child support obligation from a statutory schedule. The obligation is then divided proportionally based on each parent's share of the combined income. Adjustments are made for health insurance, childcare, and extraordinary expenses.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: Georgia's child support guidelines were substantially revised in 2007 to adopt the income shares model.

alimonyGuidelines.description: Georgia courts have broad discretion to award alimony. There is no statutory formula. The court considers the standard of living during the marriage, duration of the marriage, age and condition of the parties, financial resources of each party, time necessary for education or training, and contribution of each party to the marriage. Adultery by the party seeking alimony is an absolute bar to alimony unless the other party condoned it.
alimonyGuidelines.notes: Georgia does not have a statutory formula or durational guidelines for alimony. Awards are entirely discretionary.

court.name: Superior Court
court.description: Divorce is filed in the Superior Court of the county where the respondent resides. If the respondent is a non-resident, file in the county where the petitioner resides.
